newsitem.title: LEBANON: Bank shares rise, Solidere steady in Beirut.
newsitem.headline: Bank shares rise, Solidere steady in Beirut.

text.p: Bank shares rose on reduced turnover on Wednesday on the Beirut Stock Exchange with Banque Audi closing at $18.25 from $18.125 and Banque Libanaise pour le Commerce at $13.125 from $13.
Solidere shares were steady with Solidere A shares unchanged from Tuesday's $10.25 and B shares also unchanged from $10.75 a day earlier.
Turnover in BLC fell sharply to 6,500 shares from 16,525 on Tuesday while a total of 12,000 Audi shares changed hands against Tuesday's 25,527.
Demand for Solidere A shares remained high with 152,100 shares changing hands from 111,390 a day earlier. This compared with a daily turnover of 40-50,000 in previous weeks and 80-100,000 last week.
Lebanon Invest Bank Share Index (LIBX), introduced by Beirut finance house Lebanon Invest on Tuesday, rose 0.83 percent to 113.60.
LIBX takes its base as 100 on January 20, 1997, the day Banque Audi became the second bank traded on the Bourse.
Total BSE turnover was 170,600 shares for a value of $1,881,388 against 198,348 shares for a value of $2,148,689 on Tuesday.
There was no trade in the four other listed firms: Ciments Blancs, Ciments Libanais, Uniceramic and Eternit.
The BLOM stock index rose 0.03 percent to 897.06 and the LISPI rose 0.16 percent to 82.15.
